<!-- README.md -->

# Appkit React

React 19 forms, validation and record views connected to application-owned adapters.

## Why

Feature subpaths keep provider decisions visible while installation uses just two npm packages. Align schemas with validation and record operations; retain application control over data writes.

## Highlights

- `@alneas/appkit-react/ui`: [Compose React UI and shared providers](docs/ui.md).
- `@alneas/appkit-react/tools`: [Build schema forms and record tables](docs/tools.md).
- `@alneas/appkit-react/ai`: [Review AI proposals in React](docs/ai.md).

## Quickstart

Use an existing React 19 application with React DOM 19.

```bash
bun add @alneas/appkit-react
```

```tsx
import {Button} from '@alneas/appkit-react/ui';
import '@alneas/appkit-react/styles';
export function SaveButton() {return <Button>Save</Button>;}
```

## Next steps

[Public exports and optional peers](docs/exports.md) · [Contributing](../../CONTRIBUTING.md) · [Releasing](../../RELEASING.md)

[Complete request form](docs/request-form.md). FormView requires collection, QueryClientProvider and DataAccessProvider.

Compiled CSS license texts are retained in `THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md`.

# Review AI proposals in React

## Prerequisites

Install the package; feature subpaths are import targets.

```bash
bun add @alneas/appkit-react
```

Use React and React DOM 19 matching the package peer ranges.

## Public import

`@alneas/appkit-react/ai`

## Step-by-Step Implementation

```tsx
import * as ai from '@alneas/appkit-react/ai';
console.log(Object.keys(ai).length > 0);
```

## Verification

Type-check this example in your application. See [the export reference](exports.md) for narrower entry points and exact optional peers. Package import/type checks do not certify hosted providers.

## Troubleshooting / Common Pitfalls

React proposal review and generative UI bindings. The optional chat transport requires the ai SDK peer. Proposals do not authorize execution or stored-record changes.

## Prompt injection and review permissions

Transport text, tool-call arguments, retrieved files and tool outputs are untrusted. The optional `ai` peer is needed only by the SDK chat binding; a chat transport never approves or executes a tool. Keep provider secrets in a server-owned endpoint.

Use the [Core validation and approval sequence](../../appkit-core/docs/ai.md) before presenting a proposal. Display the exact immutable target and arguments, require explicit approval for writes or sensitive disclosure, and invalidate approval when the call, session or registration changes. The server must independently enforce resource permissions, concurrency and durable idempotency at execution time. A React component, assistant message or SDK tool-output event is not authorization.

Render registered components only, keep React text rendering escaped, and project minimal validated outputs. Do not evaluate generated code or embed arbitrary model HTML. Cancellation cannot roll back completed writes; reconcile uncertain effects before retrying. See [Core error recovery](../../appkit-core/docs/ai-errors.md).

## Application review controls

These host-owned controls consume the application's pending snapshot. Supply the Core example's controller or equivalent server-backed application flow. `onSettled` refreshes application state. No provider, database or theme provider is required just to render these controls; the larger application retains its documented providers and explicit styles.

```tsx
import {useState} from 'react';
/** Host-owned review controls; rendering or receiving a tool event never grants permission. */
export function RenameToolReview({example,pending,onSettled}:{
 example:{approve:(id:string)=>Promise<unknown>;reject:(id:string)=>void};
 pending:{approvalId:string;recordId:string;name:string}|null;onSettled:()=>void;
}){
 const [busy,setBusy]=useState(false),[failure,setFailure]=useState(false);
 if(!pending)return null;
 return <section aria-label="Review proposed rename">
  <p>Rename record {pending.recordId} to {pending.name}</p>
  <button disabled={busy} onClick={async()=>{setBusy(true);setFailure(false);try{await example.approve(pending.approvalId);}catch{setFailure(true);}finally{setBusy(false);onSettled();}}}>Approve</button>
  <button disabled={busy} onClick={()=>{example.reject(pending.approvalId);onSettled();}}>Reject</button>
  {failure&&<p role="alert">Execution could not complete. Check the application outcome before retrying.</p>}
 </section>;
}
```

---
title: "Save a schema-driven request form"
description: "Wire a schema to an application-owned adapter with retained input on failure."
archetype: how-to
project: tools
---

# Save a schema-driven request form

## Prerequisites

Install both Appkit packages and React/React DOM 19. Supply a DataAccessAdapter for your authenticated backend.

## Public import

- Form: `@alneas/appkit-react/tools/form`
- Providers: `@alneas/appkit-react/tools/data-access/react`
- Contract: `@alneas/appkit-core/data`
- CSS: `@alneas/appkit-react/styles`

## Step-by-Step Implementation

```tsx
import { useState, type ComponentProps } from 'react';
import type { DataAccessAdapter } from '@alneas/appkit-core/data';
import { QueryClientProvider } from '@tanstack/react-query';
import { createQueryClient, DataAccessProvider } from '@alneas/appkit-react/tools/data-access/react';
import { FormView } from '@alneas/appkit-react/tools/form';
import '@alneas/appkit-react/styles';

const schema: ComponentProps<typeof FormView>['schema'] = {
  type: 'object',
  properties: {
    name: { type: 'string', title: 'Name', minLength: 2 },
    reason: { type: 'string', title: 'Reason', 'x-ui': { widget: 'textarea' } },
  },
  required: ['name'],
};
export function RequestForm({ adapter }: { adapter: DataAccessAdapter }) {
  const [client] = useState(createQueryClient);
  const [saved, setSaved] = useState('');
  return <QueryClientProvider client={client}><DataAccessProvider adapter={adapter}>
    <FormView testId="persistence" collection="records" mode="create" schema={schema}
      validation={{ emptyStrings: 'preserve', locale: 'en', cast: { numericMode: 'strict' } }}
      onSuccess={record => setSaved(JSON.stringify(record))} />
    <output aria-label="Persisted">{saved}</output>
  </DataAccessProvider></QueryClientProvider>;
}
```

## Verification

Invalid names must not save; rejected saves must retain input for retry. Confirm onSuccess receives the server-confirmed result. The earlier separate-package recipe was exercised in Chromium; the consolidated packaging is checked separately. A fake adapter does not certify database persistence.

## Troubleshooting / Common Pitfalls

Keep QueryClientProvider and DataAccessProvider, including when using onSave. Authorization, migrations, version checks and durable idempotency belong on the server. Check backend semantics before retrying an operation that may already have committed.

# Build schema forms and record tables

## Prerequisites

Install the package; feature subpaths are import targets.

```bash
bun add @alneas/appkit-react
```

Use React and React DOM 19 matching the package peer ranges.

## Public import

`@alneas/appkit-react/tools`

## Step-by-Step Implementation

```tsx
import {FormView, DataTable} from '@alneas/appkit-react/tools';
import '@alneas/appkit-react/styles';
export const components = {FormView, DataTable};
```

## Verification

Type-check this example in your application. See [the export reference](exports.md) for narrower entry points and exact optional peers. Package import/type checks do not certify hosted providers.

## Troubleshooting / Common Pitfalls

Schema-driven forms, tables, filters and CRUD views. FormView requires collection, schema and mode, plus QueryClientProvider and DataAccessProvider, including when using onSave. Use the complete request-form recipe.

See [save a schema-driven request form](request-form.md) for the complete providers and persistence boundary.

# Compose React UI and shared providers

## Prerequisites

Install the package; feature subpaths are import targets.

```bash
bun add @alneas/appkit-react
```

Use React and React DOM 19 matching the package peer ranges.

## Public import

`@alneas/appkit-react/ui`

## Step-by-Step Implementation

```tsx
import {Button} from '@alneas/appkit-react/ui';
import '@alneas/appkit-react/styles';
export function SaveButton() {return <Button>Save</Button>;}
```

## Verification

Type-check this example in your application. See [the export reference](exports.md) for narrower entry points and exact optional peers. Package import/type checks do not certify hosted providers.

## Troubleshooting / Common Pitfalls

React 19 primitives, theme providers and hooks. Import CSS explicitly and share host providers. Check accessibility in the consuming application.
